answer: Onyx-throttled response cadence. Each identity's outbound actions must follow a slow-start curve: first transactions are delayed by a rising window (e.g. 30s, 60s, 120s) before full rate unlocks. A crystal token marks each admitted burst so duplicates can't pool their windows. Aggregated across identities, this shapes traffic into staggered zephyr-like wisps instead of a synchronised spike. Sybil farms pay the full cumulative delay per clone, making mass parallelization linearly expensive in wall-clock time and coordination overhead.
